text: Meaning of Life is the eighth studio album by American pop singer Kelly Clarkson, released on October 27, 2017, by Atlantic Records. Executive produced by Clarkson and Craig Kallman, it marks her debut release with the label after completing her recording contract with RCA Records, which she signed following her win on the first season of American Idol in 2002. Weary of the restrictive pop-focused structure of her prior deal, Clarkson sought to explore soul and R&B music—a genre she had long desired but had not pursued due to lack of opportunity—until being offered a long-term worldwide deal with Atlantic by Warner Music Nashville executive John Esposito, which included greater creative freedom. The album is her second foray into soul and R&B, following the lead single from her debut album "Miss Independent," and draws inspiration from the 1990s music of Aretha Franklin, Mariah Carey, Whitney Houston, En Vogue, and Bonnie Raitt, aiming to evoke a "soulful" spirit reminiscent of those artists' early works. Clarkson and Kallman commissioned a range of collaborators, including Jesse Shatkin, Greg Kurstin, Mozella, Jason Halbert, The Monarch, Mick Schultz, Harlœ, and James Morrison, with the album's tracks centered on interpersonal connections, specifically love and living in the moment. The album received generally positive critical reception, praised for Clarkson's confidence and cohesion, and debuted in the top three of the Billboard 200, marking her eighth consecutive studio album to achieve this. Three singles—"Love So Soft," "I Don't Think About You," and "Heat"—were released to promote the album, with the first and last topping the Billboard Dance Club Songs chart. "Love So Soft" earned two Grammy Award nominations: Best Pop Vocal Album and Best Pop Solo Performance at the 60th and 61st ceremonies. The album's supporting tour, Meaning of Life Tour, visited U.S. arenas between January and March 2019. After completing her seventh studio album, Piece by Piece (2015) and its companion remix album in 2016, Clarkson ended her contract with RCA Records and 19 Recordings, which held phonographic rights to her master recordings. RCA executives Peter Edge and Tom Corson offered her a three-album deal with a $1 million advance per album, contrasting with the previous six-album, $500,000-per-record agreement. Despite a successful relationship with Edge and Corson, Clarkson declined the renewal, calling it an "arranged marriage," and instead signed with Atlantic on June 24, 2016. The move reunited her with Pete Ganbarg, who had previously worked on her album All I Ever Wanted (2009), and led to her debut appearance on an Atlantic record with the Hamilton-inspired mixtape track "It's Quiet Uptown." Three of her previous producers—Greg Kurstin, Jason Halbert, and Jesse Shatkin—returned for Meaning of Life, while new collaborators included The Monarch, Nick Ruth, and Mick Schultz. Recording sessions began after her 2016 pregnancy and continued into 2017. To avoid a sound similar to Stronger (2011), Clarkson met with songwriters and showcased soulful tracks to define the album's direction. She contributed to a few songs, drawing lyrical inspiration from the novel Big Little Lies, though family life limited her writing efforts. Songwriters such as Ali Tamposi, Mozella, Harlœ, Sebastian Kole, Diztortion, and Warren "Oak" Felder submitted material in Nashville. Clarkson and Kallman jointly executive produced the album, with Kallman handling A&R, marking the first time in ten years Clarkson received executive producer credit. She described Kallman as "instrumental" in guiding the project and emphasized his role in preserving the soulful integrity of the music. Kallman personally invited the soul band Earth, Wind & Fire to perform at recording sessions for two tracks, and Clarkson requested her touring backup singers—Jessi Collins, Nicole Hurst, and Bridget Sarai—to be featured prominently, deviating from her past practice of recording her own background vocals. The album's theme is connection, with Clarkson stating that "life is about loving yourself enough so that you can love others" and that "we need to connect, we need to have conversations." She illustrated the album's logo as a circle to emphasize life's interconnectedness and that no one is in the middle of it. Clarkson emphasized that the album is not "great because of Kelly Clarkson," but because of the musicians, singers, engineers, and producers involved. Musically, the album is described as a mixture of soulful R&B pop, "soulful pop"/"pop-soul," or a soul and R&B record, with critics noting its blend of soulful anthems and empowerment pop. Atlantic promoted the album as a "sensual" pop record and her first documented soul and R&B album, while Clarkson described it as a "grown-ass woman's record" made after living life, reflecting mature themes such as emotional intimacy and self-acceptance. The album opens with "A Minute (Intro)," written and produced by The Monarch with input from Jim McCormick and Katie Pearlman, a self-care anthem for Clarkson. "Love So Soft," co-written and co-produced by Shatkin, Mozella, and Priscilla Renea, is a tribute to classic R&B. "Heat," produced by The Monarch and Mick Schultz with Harlœ and Michael Pollack, discusses full commitment in a relationship. The titular track "Meaning of Life" was written by James Morrison with Ilsey Juber and Shatkin, originally pitched for Piece by Piece but later used as a foundation for the new album. "Move You," written by Nick Ruth, Amy Kuney, and Molly Kate Kestner, bridges religious and secular music. "Whole Lotta Woman," co-written by Jussifer, Novawav duo Denisia Andrews & Brittany Coney, Fade Majah, and Shatkin, is an empowerment anthem rooted in Southern U.S. culture. Earth, Wind & Fire prominently features on this track. "Medicine," co-written and produced by Schultz and Harlœ, is inspired by Carey's "Emotions" (1991). "Cruel," written by The Monarch, Harlœ, and Pat Linehan and produced by Jason Halbert, speaks to commanding respect in a relationship. "Didn't I," written by the Davidsons, Audra Mae, and Pearlman, is a song where Clarkson bellows at a man for abandoning her. "Would You Call that Love," co-written with Greg Kurstin and produced by him, reflects on failed relationships. "I Don't Think About You," written by Harlœ, Michael Pollack, and The Monarch and produced by them, is a ballad based on a past relationship. "Slow Dance," written by Ruth, Kuney, and Kestner, is a sultry song about a woman demanding a man to take things slowly. The final two tracks, "Don't You Pretend" and "Go High," were co-written by Clarkson, Shatkin, and Mozella; the latter is inspired by Michelle Obama's 2016 Democratic National Convention speech. Originally scheduled for June 2017, the release was delayed to October 27, 2017. Atlantic's senior marketing manager Chris Ruff stated the rollout would prioritize physical sales before streaming promotion. The lead single "Love So Soft" was released digitally with "Move You" on September 7, 2017, peaked in the top fifty of the Billboard Hot 100, and topped the Billboard Dance Club Songs chart. The titular track "Meaning of Life" was released as a promotional single on October 19, 2017, followed by "I Don't Think About You" on February 9, 2018, and "Heat" on July 27, 2018. Clarkson announced the Meaning of Life Tour following her role as a coach on the fourteenth season of The Voice, with the tour visiting U.S. cities from January to March 2019. To promote the album, Clarkson performed at events including a Rainbow Room concert in New York City with Kallman, Greenwald, and Max Lousada on September 6, 2017, a "Nashville Sessions" series at the War Memorial Auditorium, an iHeartRadio Secret Session in Toronto broadcast in the following month, and an album release party in Los Angeles on the release date, aired live on iHeartRadio stations. In November 2017, she performed at two events in New York City—one hosted by Neil DeGrasse Tyson at YouTube Space and the other at the Gramercy Theatre with Sirius XM. Cracker Barrel sponsored a "Rocking and Stockings" series during the 2017 holiday season. Clarkson performed the album's songs on The Today Show, America's Got Talent, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, The Graham Norton Show, The Late Late Show with James Corden, The Voice of Germany, the 2017 We Day, the 2017 Invictus Games, the 2017 American Music Awards, Strictly Come Dancing, and other televised events.

Clarkson performed multiple selections from her album *Meaning of Life* across various televised events. She premiered "Love So Soft" on The Today Show the day after its release and performed it on programs including America's Got Talent, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, The Graham Norton Show, The Late Late Show with James Corden, The Voice of Germany, the 2017 We Day, the 2017 Invictus Games, and the 2017 American Music Awards. She performed the titular track on Strictly Come Dancing; "I Don't Think About You" on The Ellen DeGeneres Show; "Move You", "I Don't Think About You", and "Didn't I" on The Today Show; "Heat" on The Today Show and the Opening Ceremony of the 2018 US Open; "Whole Lotta Woman" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, The Late Late Show with James Corden (during Carpool Karaoke), and the 2018 Billboard Music Awards; "I Don't Think About You" and "Didn't I" on Late Night with Seth Meyers; and "Medicine" and "I Don't Think About You" on The Voice. The album received generally positive reviews from music critics, with Gold Derby's consensus stating that the "intimate, R&B-drenched album is full of confidence," describing its soul emphasis as "euphorically liberated." On Metacritic, it received an average score of 73 based on eight reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews." AllMusic's Stephen Thomas Erlewine gave it a four-star rating, calling it one of her most satisfying albums and commending Clarkson for sounding "assured here in a way that differs from her earliest records." Leah Greenblatt of Entertainment Weekly gave it a "B+" rating, noting its cohesion and self-assurance, and stating it "swings low and sweet — a refreshingly real dispatch from an artist expressing exactly what she feels in this moment." Bruner of Time wrote that the album "finds her as fans prefer: a confident artist with a sense of humor and sass to spare." Shaun Kitchener of the Daily Express rated it five stars, saying Clarkson was "in her absolute element" and the album was a "peppier, more playful alternative to Adele's 25." Glenn Gamboa of Newsday gave it a four-star rating, calling it her best album and stating it was her most cohesive work, offering a "chance to declare her ambitions and deliver on them." Isaac Feldberg of The Boston Globe noted that Clarkson "has perhaps never sounded as confident or comfortable as she does" and that she "channels her delight at [her] newfound freedom into songs that, while signaling a new stage in her career, appear to flow directly from both her heart and soul." Mike Nied of Idolator said that "returning to her roots had truly opened a wealth of opportunities" for Clarkson. Craig Jenkins of Vulture described the album as "a simmering pot of warm grooves and powerful vocals, a career pivot to the music that Clarkson ought to have been allowed to make right out of the gate." Michael Cragg of The Observer rated it four stars, comparing its sound to Meghan Trainor and Mariah Carey and crediting its "big, syrupy" ballads for "accentuating Clarkson's undeniably powerful voice, creating a comfort zone that feels genuine." Some critics were ambivalent: Hannah Davis of The Guardian gave it a three-star rating, writing that it had "lots of filler" and evoked Christina Aguilera and Trainor, but noted its "strong, '90s diva-ish mood suits Clarkson's belting vocal style" as she enters a more soulful phase. Katherine St. Asaph of Spin said much of the album felt "dated, studiously attempting to recreate an era Clarkson's long since transcended," and was puzzled by an album that sounded like "contractual winner's filler" nearly 15 years after winning the competition. *Meaning of Life* was nominated for Best Pop Vocal Album at the 61st Grammy Awards and Best Pop Solo Performance for "Love So Soft" at the 60th Grammy Awards. Both nominations made Clarkson the most-nominated artist in both categories' history, sharing the Best Pop Vocal Album record with Justin Timberlake. During promotion, she received honors including the Powerhouse Award at the 2017 Billboard Women in Music event, the Icon Award at the 2018 Radio Disney Music Awards, and a Hall of Fame induction at the 2017 Nickelodeon HALO Awards. The album was included on several publications' year-end lists. It debuted on the Billboard 200 in the United States at number two with 79,000 album-equivalent units, of which 68,000 were traditional album sales, marking Clarkson's eighth consecutive top three studio album and her third to debut at number two. It also debuted at number one on the Billboard Digital Albums chart and became her first entry on the Billboard Vinyl Albums chart. Overseas, it entered the top ten of the Billboard Canadian Albums chart and the Australian ARIA Albums Chart, attained a top twenty debut on the Official UK Albums Chart, the Irish IRMA Artist Albums Chart, and the Swiss Hitparade, and a top forty entry on the national charts of Austria, Germany, and the Netherlands. The album received a RIAA Gold certification in 2021, selling 500,000 equivalent units in the US.
